full_judgment:
10. It appears that the Anti-Corruption Commission has brought allegation under section 2(ট)(অ)  and 4(2) of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 against the executive body of the opposite party No. 1 Unipay To You Bangladesh Ltd. An after investigation charge-sheet has already been submitted against its Chairman, Managing Director, Executive Director, General Manager, Advisor and Director on 6-7-2010. On the basis of an application filed by the Assistant Director, Anti-Corruption Commission, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka freezed the bank accounts of the opposite party No. 1 against which the opposite party No. 1 being petitioner filed a revisional application being Metro Criminal Revision No. 367 of 2011 before the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka for releasing those accounts. After hearing the parties the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his order dated 14-6-2011 allowed the prayer of the petitioner (now the opposite party No. 1) and permitted to withdraw Taka 3,00,00,000 (three crore) per month for repaying the dues of the clients of the opposite party No. 1 and to meet their day to day expenditure against which this Miscellaneous Case has been filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission before this Court. 

 11. This case has a history as to that the opposite party No.1 Unipay To You, Bangladesh Ltd. was registered as Private Limited Company and started its business. After some days Bangladesh Bank by its circular MLPRO circular No.2 of 2010 dated 13-5-2010 issued under the signature of Deputy Chief Manager addressing to the Managing Directors and Chief Executives of the scheduled banks and financial institutions directing for freezing and staying the bank operation of the accounts maintained in the name of the company UNIPAY 2U (opposite party No.1) and that circular was challenged by the present opposite party No. 1 as petitioner before this Division in Writ Petition No.4187 of 2010 in which their Lordships were pleased to pass an ad-interim order staying the operation of the aforesaid circular till 7-7-2010, against which the Bangladesh Bank filed petition for leave To appeal before the Hon'ble Appellate Division for staying the ad-interim order passed by this Division and in that petition for leave To appeal the Hon'ble Judge in Chamber was pleased to stay the order of this Division on 7-6-2010 with a direction to file a regular Leave Petition failing which, the order of stay shall stand vacated. Thereafter the present opposite party No.1 Unipay To You Bangladesh Ltd. being petitioner filed an application for modification of the order dated 7-6-2010 passed by the Hon'ble Judge, in Chamber of the Appellate Division. The said application of the opposite party No. 1 was filed seeking permission to operate at least one account out of the accounts which have been freezed by the Bangladesh Bank and considering the aforesaid prayer on 9-6-2010 the learned Judge in chamber was pleased to modify the order dated 7-6-2010 as under ;- 

 13. It is further evident that in the meantime the matter has been taken up by the present petitioner the Anti-Corruption Commission and they filed the aforesaid case with the police station and after investigation having found prima-facie case the Commission submitted charge-sheet against the accused persons and thereafter the matter was sent to the competent Court for trial. It is evident from the record that in the aforesaid petition for leave To appeal the learned Judge in chamber of the Appellate Division permitted the opposite party No. 1 to withdraw Taka 3 (three) crore per month but subsequently the said petition for leave To appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution and also the Rule of the writ petition was discharged for non-prosecution. It is well settled that as the matters have been withdrawn by the parties concerned, as such, there is no existence of the ad-interim order passed by both the Divisions of the Supreme Court. It is evident from the record that the case against the opposite party No.1 along with the others is under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009. The accounts which have been freezed by the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, is the subject matter of the Criminal Case. The accused persons being petitioners earlier filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding but that application was rejected on the observation as to that from the perusal of the definitions of the money Laundering and predicate offence, it appears that the matter need to be examined by the trial Court on examination of evidence to reach a decision whether the allegation as brought against the petitioners is under Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 or not.
